name: San Marino
summary: A mountain republic surrounded by Italy, traditionally founded in 301 by a stonemason called Marinus; the oldest surviving republic, with a constitution from 1600.

knownFor.label: Captains Regent
knownFor.note: Two heads of state elected every six months.

location.value: Area 61.19 km². The page does not describe it as an enclave near Rimini in the part read.

terrain.value: Monte Titano (749 m) and surrounding hills.

climate.value: Mediterranean with cold winters on the mountain.

resources.value: Stone from Monte Titano; today tourism, banking and stamps.

disasters.value: Few natural disasters; the mountain setting suffers only occasional landslides.

urbanisation.value: Nine small municipalities (castelli), with the capital at the city of San Marino.

disease.value: Excellent health care; very long life expectancy.

migration.value: Many Sammarinese live abroad; Italians work there.

economicBase.value: Tourism contributes over 22% of GDP (about 2 million visitors in 2014); the main industries are banking, electronics and ceramics; wine and cheese are the main farm products; postage stamps sold mostly to collectors are a significant income.

tradeRoutes.value: Customs union with its larger neighbour.

wealth.value: A high-income economy, based on banking, tourism and manufacturing.

moneyAndTax.value: Uses the euro by agreement with the EU; lower taxes than Italy.

inequality.value: Moderate inequality, with a strong welfare system.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic with two Captains Regent elected every six months by the 60-member Grand and General Council.

keyRulers.value: Two Captains Regent, chosen every six months by the Grand and General Council; the first pair was nominated in 1243.

institutions.value: Grand and General Council; statutes of 1600.

stability.value: Stable for centuries; the republic has kept its independence since 301 by tradition.

eliteConflict.value: Competition among political parties, which form coalitions to govern.

armyAndTech.value: Ceremonial guards; defence by its neighbour.

majorWars.value: Occupied briefly by Cesare Borgia (1503) and by the papal legate of Ravenna (1739); bombed by Allied aircraft on 26 June 1944.

territoryChange.value: No changes to its borders since 1463.

alliancesRivals.value: Friendship treaty with Italy (1862); joined the UN in 1992.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded for this tiny state.

scienceEducation.value: University of the Republic of San Marino (1985).

openness.value: Open borders with Italy, and the euro is used.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and a cable car; the railway to Rimini closed in 1944.

artsArchitecture.value: The Three Towers and medieval old town (World Heritage Site).

socialStructure.value: Citizens and a larger group of Italian residents.

sharedIdentity.value: Pride in being the world’s oldest surviving republic.

dailyLife.value: Italian food and culture; piadina bread.

neighbours.value: Surrounded by Italy only, between the regions of Emilia-Romagna and Marche.

colonisation.value: Never colonised; Napoleon respected its independence.

riseSignals.value: Traditionally founded in AD 301 by Saint Marinus, according to its own claim.

peakPeriod.value: Uncertain; it has stayed small and independent.

declineSignals.value: None; the republic has survived for over 1,700 years by tradition.

outcome.value: San Marino continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
